messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT: cross-region routing anomalies detected. Elevated 5xx + latency for requests originating from eu-west-1 -> being routed to us-east-1 edge. Spike started ~10:12 UTC. Auto-page: @oncall
Evan: acked — i'm oncall. pulling up dashboards now.
Rohit: looking — traceroutes show EU clients hitting us-east LB IPs, geo-lookup still shows eu LB healthy.
Sam: symptoms? user-facing 5xx? latency?
Evan: both. API 95th p99 up from 180ms -> 1.2s, some 502/504s. Error ratio ~6% for eu region over last 10m.
Katie: Customer-facing impact: onboarding flows/timeouts in EU. CS flagged Acme and Brightlane. Ben (CS): both customers reporting degraded responses since ~10:15. Sending post to them now.
Rohit: check routing policy in control plane — last change was a rollout to change latency-based weights at 09:05 UTC. Could be related.
Evan: good call. Sam, can you fetch the rollout history?
Sam: grabbing.
Sam: rollout history: traffic-policy v12 -> latency-weight tweak rolled at 09:05 by infra-deploy. Canary passed. Full roll at 09:12.
Rohit: interesting — Canary passed from us-east vantage points only. Not surprised if eu vantagepoints hit different path.
Evan: question: is DNS returning eu LB IPs to EU clients? or is anycast misbehaving?
Rohit: dig from EU probe: eu.redwood.ai -> returns us-east1-alias.redwood.ai (unexpected). TTLs normal.
Katie: could a cloud provider AZ network flapping cause BGP to prefer us-east?
Sam: checking provider status pages. No major eu-west interruptions reported, but network events can be internal.
Evan: immediate mitigation options? 1) rollback traffic-policy to previous v11 2) pin eu customer traffic to eu regional endpoints (hotfix) 3) update DNS to respond with eu-only IPs with lower TTL. Thoughts?
Rohit: rollback v12 is fastest and reversible. Should restore prior routing.
Lisa: i'm ready to perform rollback, but want to confirm impact on in-flight sessions and caching.
Evan: do it. call it a rollback + monitor for 10m, then escalate to provider if persists.
Sam: executing rollback command: `infractl traffic-policy set --name global-routing --version v11`
Sam: rollback initiated.
IncidentBot: ACTION: rollout rollback started by Sam at 10:28 UTC (runbook: cross-region-routing rollback).
Rohit: monitoring routes and backend metrics.
Evan: watch for error ratio drop and p99 latency dropping in eu. Also watch for cache/KV errors.
Katie: notified legal/comms to prepare a brief for affected customers. Ben (CS) is on patch.
Ben (CS): I posted an update to Acme and Brightlane: "we are aware of increased latencies, engineering is rolling back a routing change; we'll update in 15 minutes." They've acknowledged.
Sam: rollback completed at 10:31. Confirming control plane accepted v11.
Rohit: traceroutes from EU probes now resolve to eu LB IPs. Good sign.
Evan: metrics — error ratio down from 6% -> 0.7% in 4 minutes. p99 back to ~210ms.
Katie: great. keep monitoring for at least 30 min.
Lisa: starting post-rollback checks: edge health, KV cache hit rates, and canary traces.
Rohit: one red flag: some EU nodes still showing traces to us-east. Looks like stale DNS caches at some ISPs. Might take time to fully converge.
Evan: mitigation for that tail: we can add a targeted edge-rule to explicitly reject/redirect requests with unwanted geolocation header to eu endpoints. But that will be riskier. Hold for now.
Sam: also looking at the latency-weight algorithm — there's a bug where small sample size from EU can cause weight skew toward us-east. I'll open a ticket.
Sam: created INF-6734 "latency-weight policy misroute on low-sample populations". Assigned to infra-routing squad.
Rohit: root cause hypothesis: policy v12 used improved latency signals but did not properly account for geo-sampled metrics, so eu samples underweighted eu LB causing cross-region selection.
Evan: good hypothesis. Next steps: 1) postmortem draft, 2) patch policy algorithm, 3) add EU-only canary checks, 4) update runbook to require geo-vantage canary.
Katie: assigned postmortem. I'll coordinate with product and comms.
Ben (CS): customer follow-up being queued. We'll ask for any error logs and list of affected timelines.
Lisa: note for SLA/metrics: tag requests during incident with incident id INC-20240315-1 for billing/analysis.
Evan: can we confirm if any Dedicated or Private customers were affected?
Rohit: querying membership -> Dedicated clusters in eu were unaffected (they bypass global routing), but hosted customers using global API were affected.
Ben (CS): reached out to biggest affected customer, they'll want an RCA.
Sam: timeline: 09:05 policy roll v12 -> 10:12 anomalies detected -> 10:28 rollback started -> 10:31 rollback completed -> 10:36 metrics normalizing -> 11:05 closing watch.
Evan: i'm handing over monitoring to Rohit for the rest of the shift. I'm going offline in 20. Rohit, you good to own watch?
Rohit: taking watch. If anything spikes, page me on pager duty.
Ben (CS): will send customer follow-up at 11:00 with summary and next steps.
Katie: postmortem owner assigned: Katie. Target draft in 48 hours.
Sam: added short-term mitigations to infra backlog: INF-6735 (DNS low-TTL emergency switch), INF-6736 (edge-rule redirect option), INF-6734 (policy fix).
IncidentBot: INCIDENT NOTE: severity set to S2. Customers impacted: multiple hosted API customers in EU. Estimated impacted fraction: ~5-8% of EU-origin requests during window.
Evan: closing note: major rollback resolved customer impact quickly. Root cause likely policy misroute due to sampling. We need better geo canaries. Closing watch handed to Rohit.
Rohit: will run extra validation at 11:10 and post final status.
Ben (CS): customers acknowledged the update and appreciate quick mitigation.
Katie: thanks everyone. filing postmortem soon. :thumbsup:
